metadata.description: Full human review of the flat classification script's (map_state_to_ccss.py) output against every code it did NOT trivially agree on with a prior hand-built mapping -- 25 of the script's 150 GA codes, each independently re-examined against the actual GA and CCSS standard text. 8 verdicts came back 'error' (the script's own classification was wrong; `human_corrected_to` gives the corrected relationship/codes, now baked into runs/ga/mapping_final.json). The other 17 came back 'okay' -- a defensible judgment call, or the script's answer stands as the better one; the script's original output was kept unchanged for those. Combined with 142 codes that needed no review at all, this means 142/150 (95%) of the script's raw output required no correction whatsoever.

ccss_codes.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

ccss_codes.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.
